description: A node's own AI stack, as committed config: its own model server (Ollama) and its own chat surface (Open WebUI), the declarative slice of adoption item 3 in CLUSTER_INFERENCE_DESIGN.md. Read by peer-node/tests/test_node_ai_stack.py, which fails the build if the committed topology stops being the loopback-only, own-server-only, no-authority surface the design requires. Cluster fan-out is NOT here: accepting a signed subtask belongs to the task ingress + cluster client (item 5), so nothing in this file can be a vector for delegated inference.

topology.why_loopback_only: A node's own prompts never leave the node's containers. Only a served subtask crosses the overlay, and no subtask can arrive here until item 5. Binding 0.0.0.0 would put the node's knowledge on every interface at once.

gpu.why: GPU is never required to run, only to change throughput. The committed file declares none; the host deployer adds a device reservation on a node that has one. Docker cannot partition VRAM, so GPU sharing is configured inside the model server, never by slicing containers.

open_webui_rag.why: Open WebUI's own vector store would become a second, grant-less knowledge base — the same rule as the Master admin surface. A parallel store cannot be revoked with a signed entry, which makes it the quieter way to lose control of what the fabric knows.

capabilities.why: A node's own prompts are already free and need no capability (COMPUTE_CAPABILITY_DESIGN.md draws the same line: only delegated work is gated). 'cluster-serve' is what a *delegated subtask* would need, and no subtask can reach this stack until item 5; 'sign' belongs to the Master alone and is structurally unobtainable here — the stack mounts no key, no signer socket and no $SPARKNET_STATE_DIR.

webui_surface.declared_not_database_state: Open WebUI's panel is a database click; the surface lives in agent-models.json + this compose env so a redeploy cannot lose it (peer PLAN Step 5 DoD 5).
webui_surface.bridge_route: OPENAI_API_BASE_URLS=http://host.docker.internal:4096/v1 — this node's dispatch bridge, loopback 4096, reached through extra_hosts host.docker.internal:host-gateway. Live reachability from the webui container past the bridge's loopback gate is a target-node check (DoD: confirm: user), like the rest of this stack.
webui_surface.bridge_key: OPENAI_API_KEYS expands a deploy-time signed grant ($SPARKNET_WEBUI_BRIDGE_GRANT); no token is committed and the compose fails loudly while it is unset.
webui_surface.approve_deny: a permission request surfaces as an Approve/Deny card and resolves through POST /session/:id/permissions/:permissionID on the dispatch bridge (peer PLAN Step 5 DoD 2); the decision is recorded in the grant-keyed session.
webui_surface.rag: still disabled (RAG_INGESTION_ENABLED=false) — the vault is the only knowledge base (peer PLAN Step 5 DoD 4).

conversation_passing.contract: the /session/:id native verbs on the dispatch bridge (peer PLAN Step 6)
conversation_passing.message: POST /session/:id/message accepts an 'agent' and hands the conversation off with history intact (Step 6 DoD 1)
conversation_passing.fork: POST /session/:id/fork at a message index creates a child session carrying the shared prefix; the original stays whole (Step 6 DoD 2)
conversation_passing.children_and_shares: GET /session/:id/children lists the branch; POST/GET/DELETE /session/:id/share[/:id] declare a session-view/session-handoff share in 'open' status (Step 6 DoD 3)
conversation_passing.native_primitives: only native opencode/OpenAI verbs; no custom passing mechanism (Step 6 note)
conversation_passing.regime_not_here: clocks, expiry, cross-node transfer and the kb-*/full share kinds belong to Step 8 and are deliberately absent

masterspike.artifacts: Modelfile + vllm-system-prompt.md, both generated from the one source by scripts/sparknet-masterspike.py (peer PLAN Step 7 DoD 1/2); `make model-verify` fails on divergence or a moved source (DoD 3)
masterspike.selectable: masterspike is in agent-models.json and MODEL_FILTER_LIST (DoD 4)
masterspike.capability_boundary: the model holds no signing capability — the artifacts are text with no key, no signer socket and no state dir, and authority stays Ed25519 in the Master, never a prompt (DoD 4)

signing_boundary.why_structural: A deny rule governs a process that may later ignore it. This stack is declared without the mounts a key or a socket would need, which makes the boundary structural rather than a permission statement.

not_built_yet: This is a declaration, not a deployment. No model server or Open WebUI is installed on this host, no image is pulled, and nothing binds 11434 or 8080; the MASTERSPIKE Ollama model is likewise not created (this host has an `ollama` binary but no running daemon — `make model-build` will refuse with Ollama's own error until one is served). The deployed healthcheck — pull the images on a target node, run the stack, confirm the surfaces answer with no GPU present, create and serve the model — is `DoD: confirm: user`. The assertions in test_node_ai_stack.py and test_masterspike.py are read off these files, the compose file and the generated artifacts, and are therefore only as strong as the files: they prove the declared topology and the artifacts are coherent, not that a real deployment held.
